context_purpose: Employer HR confirms an absence is medically justified for specific dates before approving paid sick leave.

norm_violation_today.reason: HR needs only unfit-for-work dates but receives diagnosis, procedure and ward, which exceeds the leave-approval norm.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Cannot support disputes about the medical reason, insurer claims, or a manager's request for recovery detail.

transmission_check.reason: Employee hands over the certificate to get paid leave; whether work rules or insurers require the diagnosis certificate is not something I can state for Taiwan.

context_purpose: Landlord wants assurance the tenant can still pay rent at renewal.

norm_violation_today.reason: Re-collecting salary, employer and full ID copy at renewal goes beyond a yes/no on current employment.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Landlord cannot judge income level or job type, which many landlords actually want.

transmission_check.reason: No law obliges a private landlord to collect payslips, so a narrower proof is allowed if the landlord accepts it.

context_purpose: University checks a student is eligible to work and is approved for the position before payroll.

norm_violation_today.reason: Payroll is entitled to passport/ARC data, but department staff who only approve the hire also collect and store copies.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Payroll still needs the underlying identifiers and copies for payment and labour inspection.

transmission_check.reason: As employer the university appears obliged to keep work-permit and ARC records, so proofs only limit internal access, not retention.

context_purpose: Landlord assesses whether a tenant has a record of paying rent on time.

norm_violation_today.reason: Full statements expose balances, payees and unrelated transfers when only a payment-regularity fact is needed.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Misses rent paid in cash or from other banks and cannot show the tenant's wider finances, deposits or guarantor strength.

transmission_check.reason: Landlord requests statements by habit with no legal duty, so a narrower proof is acceptable if trusted.

context_purpose: Landlord or subsidy office confirms the tenant is the enrolled student who qualifies for student-rate or subsidised housing.

norm_violation_today.reason: Full ID copy, parents' contacts and home address go well beyond confirming enrolment of the same person.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Landlord still wants a real address and guarantor, and a subsidy office may need the actual ID number.

transmission_check.reason: Student hands documents over to obtain the rate or subsidy; whether the subsidy office must hold the full ID number is not clear to me.

context_purpose: Rental operator judges the reliability of a renter to waive or reduce a deposit.

norm_violation_today.reason: Whole-account screenshots reveal name, photo, addresses and trip history when only rating and trip count matter.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Rating says little about driving skill, and a licence check is still needed.

transmission_check.reason: Deposit waiver is the operator's own business choice, no law requires the screenshot.

context_purpose: Travel agency avoids taking deposits from travellers who legally cannot leave the country.

norm_violation_today.reason: Full ID and passport copies are kept at deposit stage though only absence from the restriction register is being checked.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Agency still needs passport details later for tickets and visas, so the saving is only at the deposit stage.

transmission_check.reason: Checking is the agency's own risk management, but whether the immigration agency may confirm restriction status at all is unclear to me.

context_purpose: Platform or city procurement clerk confirms a small seller or bidder has no overdue tax cases.

norm_violation_today.reason: Clearance certificates carry ID number and often tax detail beyond a no-overdue-case fact.

purpose_sufficiency.lost: Nothing material beyond an as-of date, unless procurement rules name the paper certificate.

transmission_check.reason: Procurement may require a named certificate and tax secrecy may limit what the bureau signs; I cannot say which applies, while marketplace onboarding is likely voluntary.
